Before you begin

  1. Show the full body in frame
  2. Keep one person in view with good light
  3. Use replay to test a possible-fall alert safely

Possible-fall detection is a heuristic and will make mistakes. It is not a diagnosis. Lying down on purpose can trigger an alert.

Offline preparation

Preparing offline shell…

Replay, alerts, journal and saved research work offline after caching. The camera model needs a separate download. Camera Coach needs a connection. Browser storage may be cleared or evicted.

Session events

Research with a source

Ask about exercise, sleep, isolation, teamwork or OSDR datasets. Answers come only from a small curated NASA library. In Live mode your question and the retrieved passages go to Meta; camera observations and journal entries are never attached.

Checking research service…

General information only. Not medical advice or emergency guidance.

Prepared questions · also available offline

Explore NASA OSDR datasets ↗

OSDR study descriptions are research records, not personal health guidance. MUSE uses curated text; the historical dataset charts on the dashboard are separate. Independent source review is pending.

New entry

Entries stay in this browser. Theme summaries and optional sentiment feedback describe your words, not your health.

About the sentiment dataset

Uses human-rated English words from the VADER lexicon with a custom wording heuristic, not the full VADER algorithm. Sarcasm, quotations and context can change the meaning. No clinical or astronaut-wellness validation. Nothing you write is uploaded.
